461	    @staticmethod
462	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
463	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
464	
465	        The very same mutual-ownership requirement backs direct construction
466	        and checkpoint loading, so it lives in exactly one place. The binding
467	        only governs work still in progress:
468	
469	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
470	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
471	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
472	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
473	          collected additionally must have an owner.
474	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
475	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
476	
477	        Completed tasks only keep *historical* ownership: their recorded
478	        ``assigned_robot`` is not required to be idle or to name them back, so
479	        a robot that already finished one task may be idle or busy with a new
480	        one. Unassigned, not-yet-collected tasks simply wait -- even when no
481	        robot can reach them -- and are not an ownership error. Nothing here
482	        rewrites a binding or drops a task; an inconsistent input is rejected
483	        as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the conflicting robot or
484	        task, leaving the caller's objects untouched.
485	        """
486	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
487	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
488	        for robot in robots:
489	            if robot.task_id is None:
490	                continue
491	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
492	            if task is None:
493	                raise ValueError(
494	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
495	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
496	                )
497	            if task.completed:
498	                raise ValueError(
499	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
500	                    "that is already completed"
501	                )
502	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
503	                raise ValueError(
504	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
505	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
506	                )
507	        for task in tasks:
508	            # Completed tasks retain historical ownership; their robots are
509	            # free to take new work, so the mutual binding only holds while a
510	            # task is still in progress.
511	            if task.completed:
512	                continue
513	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
514	                raise ValueError(
515	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
516	                )
517	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
518	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
519	                if owner is None:
520	                    raise ValueError(
521	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
522	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
523	                    )
524	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
525	                    raise ValueError(
526	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
527	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
528	                    )

530	    @staticmethod
531	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
532	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
533	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
534	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
535	
536	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound, via the single shared walk
537	        validator :func:`_validate_route_walk` -- the same coordinate shape,
538	        map-walkability and one-orthogonal-step rule checkpoint recovery uses
539	        -- so a walking rule never has to be changed in two places. The outer
540	        route may be a list or tuple and each waypoint may itself be a list or
541	        tuple of two plain integers -- booleans are not integers here, and
542	        wrong lengths or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of
543	        leaking unpacking or hashing failures. The forms may be mixed freely;
544	        only the coordinate order matters, not the container types.
545	
546	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
547	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
548	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
549	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
550	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
551	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
552	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
553	
554	        The check is read-only -- :func:`_validate_route_walk` builds fresh
555	        lists, and the caller commits them itself only once every robot has
556	        passed, so a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a
557	        later robot or at the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders
558	        or otherwise modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. The
559	        shared walk check says nothing about tasks; direct construction keeps
560	        accepting any walkable route, while checkpoint loading keeps its own
561	        stricter validation that also covers the pickup/dropoff rules.
562	        """
563	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
564	        for robot in robots:
565	            route = robot.route
566	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
567	                raise ValueError(
568	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
569	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
570	                )
571	            normalized.append(
572	                _validate_route_walk(
573	                    grid,
574	                    robot.position,
575	                    route,
576	                    robot_id=robot.robot_id,
577	                    checkpoint=False,
578	                )
579	            )
580	        return normalized

582	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
583	    # Dynamic map edits
584	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

586	    def modify_obstacles(
587	        self,
588	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
589	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
590	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
591	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
592	
593	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
594	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
595	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
596	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
597	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
598	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
599	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
600	
601	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
602	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
603	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
604	        distance is accumulated.
605	        """
606	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
607	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
608	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
609	        if conflict:
610	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
611	            raise ValueError(
612	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
613	            )
614	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
615	        for cell in add_cells:
616	            if cell in occupied:
617	                raise ValueError(
618	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
619	                )
620	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
621	
622	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
623	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
624	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
625	        seen: set[Position] = set()
626	        ordered: list[Position] = []
627	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
628	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
629	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
630	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
631	            if position in seen:
632	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
633	                continue
634	            seen.add(position)
635	            ordered.append(position)
636	        return ordered
637	
638	    def _apply_map_change(
639	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
640	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
641	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
642	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
643	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
644	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
645	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
646	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
647	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
648	
649	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
650	        # known to change the map.
651	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
652	        self._map_sequence += 1
653	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
654	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
655	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
656	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
657	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
658	        return copy.deepcopy(record)

660	    def _map_change_record(
661	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
662	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
663	        return {
664	            "type": "map_change",
665	            "tick": self.tick,
666	            "sequence": sequence,
667	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
668	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
669	        }

671	    def _plan_route(
672	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
673	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
674	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
675	
676	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
677	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
678	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
679	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
680	        """
681	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
682	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
683	
684	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
685	        for task in self.tasks.values():
686	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
687	                continue
688	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
689	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
690	                continue
691	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
692	            if route is None:
693	                robot.route = []
694	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
695	            else:
696	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
697	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
698	                robot.route = route
699	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
700	
701	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
702	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
703	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
704	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
705	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
706	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
707	                continue
708	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
709	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
710	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
711	                continue
712	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
713	            if route is None:
714	                robot.route = []
715	                continue
716	            robot.route = route
717	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
718	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

724	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
725	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
726	        cells: set[Position] = set()
727	        for robot in self.robots.values():
728	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
729	                cells.update(robot.route)
730	        return cells
731	
732	    def _safe_side_cells(
733	        self,
734	        robot: Robot,
735	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
736	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
737	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
738	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
739	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
740	
741	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
742	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
743	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
744	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
745	
746	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
747	          skips anything else),
748	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
749	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
750	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
751	          route is excluded), and
752	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
753	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
754	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
755	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
756	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
757	
758	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
759	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
760	        """
761	        blocked = set(forbidden)
762	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
763	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
764	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
765	                continue
766	            yield cell

768	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
769	        self,
770	        blocker: Robot,
771	        requester: Robot,
772	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
773	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
774	    ) -> Position | None:
775	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
776	
777	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
778	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
779	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
780	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
781	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
782	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
783	        """
784	        return next(
785	            self._safe_side_cells(
786	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
787	            ),
788	            None,
789	        )

791	    def _self_sidestep(
792	        self,
793	        robot: Robot,
794	        task: Task | None,
795	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
796	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
797	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
798	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
799	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
800	
801	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
802	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
803	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
804	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
805	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
806	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
807	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
808	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
809	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
810	        """
811	        if task is None or task.completed:
812	            return None
813	        destination = robot.route[0]
814	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
815	        if blocker_id is None:
816	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
817	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
818	        best_length = 0
819	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
820	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
821	        # that order as the tie break.
822	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
823	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
824	            if route is None:
825	                continue
826	            if (
827	                blocker_id is not None
828	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
829	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
830	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
831	                )
832	            ):
833	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
834	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
835	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
836	                continue
837	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
838	                best = (cell, route)
839	                best_length = len(route)
840	        return best
841	
842	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
843	        self,
844	        robot: Robot,
845	        side: Position,
846	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
847	        blocker_id: str,
848	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
849	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
850	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
851	    ) -> bool:
852	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
853	
854	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
855	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
856	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
857	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
858	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
859	        never rejected here.
860	        """
861	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
862	            return False
863	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
864	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
865	            return False
866	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
867	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
868	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
869	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
870	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
871	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
872	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
873	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
874	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
875	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
876	        return not self._can_vacate(
877	            blocker,
878	            robot,
879	            hyp_occupied,
880	            reserved,
881	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
882	            blocked_path,
883	        )
884	
885	    def _can_vacate(
886	        self,
887	        blocker: Robot,
888	        requester: Robot,
889	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
890	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
891	        checking: frozenset[str],
892	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
893	    ) -> bool:
894	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
895	
896	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
897	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
898	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
899	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
900	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
901	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
902	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots already on the
903	        dependency chain (including robots that used their one move of this
904	        tick), so meeting one again closes a cyclic dependency -- a head-on
905	        deadlock, or the requester itself -- and never proves an exit merely
906	        because every robot on the cycle still carries a route.
907	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
908	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
909	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
910	        the blocker's own route does).
911	
912	        The follow chain can run through an arbitrarily long legal queue, so
913	        the search is an explicit stack rather than Python recursion: a queue
914	        of twelve hundred robots ending at a parked robot with no side cell
915	        must report "cannot vacate" from a normal ``step()`` instead of
916	        raising :class:`RecursionError`. Each frame is
917	        ``(robot, checking, resume)``. A frame examined for the first time
918	        first tries the free-waypoint and follow-chain rules; only when the
919	        chain ahead comes back empty does it resume at its own side-cell
920	        scan, which is exactly the order the single recursive call imposed.
921	        """
922	        stack: list[tuple[Robot, frozenset[str], bool]] = [(blocker, checking, False)]
923	        while stack:
924	            current, current_checking, resume = stack.pop()
925	            if current.robot_id in current_checking:
926	                # The chain has folded back onto a robot it already depends
927	                # on: a cycle cannot vacate itself. The frame that followed
928	                # this one simply resumes with its own side-cell options.
929	                continue

950	                if (
951	                    self.grid.traversable(ahead)
952	                    and ahead not in occupied
953	                    and ahead not in reserved
954	                ):
955	                    return True
956	                occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
957	                if (

959	                    and occupant_id != current.robot_id
960	                    and occupant_id not in current_checking

968	                        (
969	                            self.robots[occupant_id],
970	                            current_checking | {current.robot_id},

972	                        )

990	    def _update_traffic_waits(
991	        self,
992	        waited: dict[str, str],
993	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
994	    ) -> None:
995	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
996	
997	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
998	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
999	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
1000	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
1001	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
1002	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
1003	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
1004	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
1005	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
1006	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
1007	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
1008	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
1009	        """
1010	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1011	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
1012	        for robot_id in waited:
1013	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
1014	                continue
1015	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
1016	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1017	                continue
1018	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
1019	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1020	                continue
1021	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
1022	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
1023	                continue
1024	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
1025	            if entry is None:
1026	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
1027	            else:
1028	                surviving[robot_id] = {
1029	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
1030	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
1031	                }
1032	        self._traffic_waits = surviving

1034	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
1035	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
1036	
1037	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
1038	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
1039	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
1040	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
1041	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
1042	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
1043	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
1044	        """
1045	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1046	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
1047	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
1048	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1049	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
1050	                continue
1051	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
1052	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]

1054	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
1055	        return [
1056	            {
1057	                "robot_id": robot_id,
1058	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
1059	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
1060	            }
1061	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
1062	        ]

1068	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
1069	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest available robot using stable tie breaks.
1070	
1071	        Only a robot with no bound task *and* no remaining route is available:
1072	        a taskless robot still driving a preset route keeps that route and is
1073	        never selected, even when it is the closest to the pickup -- being
1074	        temporarily blocked by traffic does not count as having finished the
1075	        route either. Skipping such a robot never touches its position,
1076	        mileage, cargo state or remaining waypoints, and never makes other
1077	        tasks wait: the next available robot is chosen by the usual shortest
1078	        feasible route length with the robot id string as tie break.
1079	        """
1080	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
1081	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
1082	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
1083	            for robot in self.robots.values():
1084	                if not robot.idle or robot.route:
1085	                    continue
1086	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
1087	                if route is None:
1088	                    continue
1089	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
1090	            if not choices:
1091	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
1092	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
1093	                continue
1094	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
1095	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
1096	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
1097	            robot.route = route
1098	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id

1101	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
1102	        for robot in self.robots.values():
1103	            if robot.task_id is None:
1104	                continue
1105	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
1106	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
1107	                task.picked_up = True

1109	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:

1111	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
1112	        self.assign_tasks()
1113	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
1114	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
1115	        self._confirm_pickups()
1116	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1117	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
1118	        moved: list[str] = []
1119	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
1120	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
1121	
1122	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
1123	            del occupied[robot.position]
1124	            robot.position = destination
1125	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
1126	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
1127	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
1128	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
1129	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
1130	
1131	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
1132	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
1133	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
1134	                continue
1135	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
1136	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1137	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
1138	                continue
1139	            if not robot.route:
1140	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1141	                continue
1142	            destination = robot.route[0]
1143	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
1144	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
1145	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
1146	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
1147	                    if route is None:
1148	                        robot.route = []
1149	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
1150	                    else:
1151	                        robot.route = route
1152	                continue
1153	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
1154	            if blocker_id is None:
1155	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
1156	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
1157	                relocate(robot, destination)
1158	                robot.route.pop(0)
1159	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1160	                continue
1161	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
1162	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
1163	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
1164	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:

1166	                    # Truly parked blocker: no bound task and no remaining
1167	                    # route. Ask it to yield onto a free side cell, then take
1168	                    # over the cell it vacated. A taskless robot that still has
1169	                    # a remaining route is not parked: it drives that route
1170	                    # cell by cell like any other moving robot and is never
1171	                    # pushed off it for a requester.
1172	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
1173	                    if side is not None:

1175	                        relocate(robot, destination)
1176	                        robot.route.pop(0)
1177	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1178	                        continue
1179	                if blocker.route:
1180	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
1181	                    if (
1182	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
1183	                        and ahead not in occupied
1184	                        and ahead not in reserved
1185	                    ):

1191	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
1192	            side = self._self_sidestep(

1194	            )

1198	                robot.route = route
1199	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1200	                continue
1201	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
1202	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
1203	        self.tick += 1
1204	        event: dict[str, object] = {
1205	            "type": "tick",
1206	            "tick": self.tick,
1207	            "moved": moved,
1208	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
1209	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),

1271	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
1272	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
1273	        raise :class:`OSError`.
1274	        """
1275	        document = {
1276	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
1277	            "grid": {
1278	                "width": self.grid.width,
1279	                "height": self.grid.height,
1280	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
1281	            },
1282	            "base_grid": {
1283	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
1284	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
1285	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
1286	            },
1287	            "tick": self.tick,
1288	            "robots": [
1289	                {
1290	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
1291	                    "position": list(robot.position),
1292	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
1293	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
1294	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
1295	                }
1296	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
1297	            ],
1298	            "tasks": [
1299	                {
1300	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
1301	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
1302	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
1303	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
1304	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
